questions.q: Match each event to the curve it shifts first.
pairs: A big rise in the skills of the workforce
questions.why: Spending moves AD, costs move SRAS and capacity moves LRAS.

questions.q: Underlying economic growth is shown by:
options: A rise in the price level

questions.q: A negative supply-side shock will cause:
options: A higher price level and lower real output
A lower price level and higher real output
A higher price level and higher real output
questions.why: SRAS shifts left, so prices and unemployment worsen together.

questions.q: A change in the price level shifts the AD curve.
questions.why: It causes a movement along the curve.

questions.q: Explain how a recession in the UK's main trading partners could lead to unemployment in the UK.

ideas.label: UK exports fall, so AD falls
UK firms produce less, so they need fewer workers

questions.model: Foreigners buy fewer UK exports, so AD falls. UK firms produce less and need fewer workers, which causes demand-deficient unemployment.
questions.why: Global events reach the UK through trade.

tests.answer: Exports fall, so AD falls and firms need fewer workers.
